nodes.name: NF@CoFeP
aliases: honeycomb-like Co2P-Fe2P nanosheets on nickel foam

nodes.name: Coprecipitation of CoFe-PBA on NF
nodes.procedure: An aqueous solution containing [Fe(CN)5NO]2- mixes with another aqueous solution containing Co2+ to self-assemble into honeycomb-like CoFe-based PBA nanosheets in the presence of NF (NF@CoFe-PBA) during the coprecipitation process.
nodes.source_text: Figure 1a exhibits the preparation process of NF@CoFeP. Typically, an aqueous solution containing [Fe(CN)5NO]2- mixes with another aqueous solution containing Co2+ to self-assemble into honeycomb-like CoFe-based PBA nanosheets in the presence of NF (NF@CoFe-PBA) during the coprecipitation process...

nodes.name: Low-temperature phosphating
nodes.procedure: The NF@CoFe-PBA precursor subsequently experienced a simple low-temperature phosphating process to give the NF@CoFeP sample. NF@CoFeP shows two obvious P 1s and P 2p characteristic peaks. The atomic ratio of P to metal atoms (Fe + Co + Ni) in NF@CoFeP is 2.2.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The NF@CoFe-PBA precursor subsequently experienced a simple low-temperature phosphating process

nodes.source_text: The NF@CoFe-PBA precursor subsequently experienced a simple low-temperature phosphating process to give the NF@CoFeP sample. ... The atomic ratio of P to metal atoms (Fe + Co + Ni) in NF@CoFeP is 2.2.

nodes.name: NF@CoFeP
aliases: honeycomb-like ultrathin and heterogeneous Co₂P-Fe₂P nanosheets on nickel foam

nodes.source_text: Figure 3a shows the HER polarization curves of NF@CoFeP... NF@CoFeP (80 mV) ... Tafel plots show that NF@CoFeP has a Tafel slope of 67 mV dec⁻¹ ... NF@CoFeP has a smaller charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of 0.81 Ω

NF@CoFeP has an OER potential of 1.52 V at 50 mA cm⁻², superior to those of NF@FeP (1.54 V), NF@P (1.68 V), and NF@Ir/C (1.61 V). The Tafel slope of NF@CoFeP is also lower than those of reference samples

nodes.source_text: NF@CoFeP||NF@CoFeP exhibits higher water-splitting performance than NF@Ir/C||NF@Pt/C. The cell voltages ... reach as low as 1.45 V at 10 mA cm⁻², 1.66 V at 100 mA cm⁻², and 1.79 V at 500 mA cm⁻² ... symmetrical NF@CoFeP||NF@CoFeP device has a larger and more stable current density to drive water electrolysis at a cell voltage of 2 V

NF@CoFeP shows the best HER performance (-82 mV at 10 mA cm⁻²)... Tafel slope of NF@CoFeP (60 mV dec⁻¹)... NF@CoFeP has the smallest R_ct of 4.5 Ω among the TMP samples... NF@CoFeP has the largest C_dl value of 17.3 mF cm⁻²
The overpotential of NF@CoFeP at 50 mA cm⁻² is 0.36 V... NF@CoFeP has the smallest R_ct of 27.4 Ω among the TMP samples at 1.50 V
NF@CoFeP has a potential of -108 mV at 10 mA cm⁻² for the HER in neutral media
NF@CoFeP shows better performance, including a smaller overpotential of 0.73 V at 50 mA cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM imaging shows honeycomb-like structure inherited from NF@CoFe-PBA precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b shows a typical SEM image of NF@CoFeP, inheriting the structure of its NF@CoFe-PBA precursor and also showing a honeycomb-like structure.

properties.description: High-resolution scanning electron microscopy image showing nanostructured material with interconnected porous network and sheet-like morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Scanning TEM image and EDS element mapping show uniform distribution of P, Co, and Fe in CoFeP nanosheet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning TEM image and the corresponding EDS element mapping of (d) P, (e) Co, and (f) Fe in a CoFeP nanosheet of NF@CoFeP.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM reveals CoFeP nanosheet thickness of around 4.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The thickness of the CoFeP nanosheets is around 4.5 nm, as revealed by atomic force microscopy (Figure 1g and Figure S4).

properties.description: Microscopy image (likely TEM or HRTEM) with scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM with FFT identifies nanocrystalline domains of Co2P (0.222 nm and 0.166 nm lattice spacings) and Fe2P species in CoFeP nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: One nanocrystalline domain marked by the red area has three clear lattice spacings of 0.222, 0.222, and 0.166 nm according to fast Fourier transformation (FFT), respectively attributed to the Co2P (¯12I), (¯12I), and (¯040) planes... Likewise, Fe2P species are explicitly identified in the CoFeP nanosheet (Figure 1j,k).

properties.description: TEM or SAED image with indexed diffraction spots

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of Co2P, Fe2P, and Ni5P4 species in addition to Ni substrate peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The rest of the characteristic peaks with relatively weak signals are ascribed to the Co2P, Fe2P, and Ni5P4 species.

properties.peaks: Multiple diffraction peaks with marked phases

nodes.characterization_summary: P 2p peaks at 129.3, 130.1 eV (M-P bonds) and 134.0 eV (P-O); Co 2p shows Co2+/Co3+ at 780.6/782.6 eV (2p3/2), 795.8/798.0 eV (2p1/2); Fe 2p shows Fe2+/Fe3+; atomic P:(Fe+Co+Ni) ratio = 2.2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks located at 129.3 and 130.1 eV are attributed to metal-P bonds including Fe-P, Co-P, and Ni-P while 134.0 eV originates from P-O bond... The atomic ratio of P to metal atoms (Fe + Co + Ni) in NF@CoFeP is 2.2.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows no phase change during HER (phosphides remain active); alkaline OER shows reconstruction to CoFe oxyhydroxides with peaks at 473.0 and 552.4 cm^{-1}; no oxyhydroxide signals in acidic OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No signal change was observed during the HER... Under alkaline conditions, two peaks at 473.0 and 552.4 cm^{-2} from metal-O vibrations in metal-OOH appear... Different from alkaline OER, no signal of oxyhydroxides was detected under acidic conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct of 0.81 Ω for HER and smaller Rct for OER compared to controls.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NF@CoFeP has a smaller charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 0.81 Ω, further illustrating its faster Faradaic process and HER kinetics.
